questions.stem: X ~ N(50, 16). The z-score of 58 is…
questions.incorrectFeedback: Divide by the SD, not the variance: σ = √16 = 4, so z = 8/4 = 2.

questions.stem: X and Y are independent, Var(X) = 9 and Var(Y) = 16. The SD of X − Y is…
questions.correctFeedback: Yes — the variances add: 9 + 16 = 25, so the SD is 5.
questions.incorrectFeedback: For independent variables the variances add even for a difference: Var(X − Y) = 25, SD = 5.

questions.stem: For any normal, P(μ − 2σ < X < μ + 2σ) is about…
questions.incorrectFeedback: Within 2 SDs a normal holds about 95% (0.9545). 75% is only Chebyshev's guarantee for any shape.

questions.stem: From Lesson 7: for any distribution at all, the share within 2σ of the mean is…
questions.correctFeedback: Right — Chebyshev: at least 1 − 1/2² = 3/4. The normal's 95% is far above that floor.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Chebyshev guarantees at least 1 − 1/k² = 3/4 within 2σ, for every shape. 95% is the normal's own figure.

questions.stem: X₁, X₂ are independent copies of X ~ N(μ, σ²). Which has the larger variance?
questions.correctFeedback: Yes — Var(2X) = 4σ², but Var(X₁ + X₂) = σ² + σ² = 2σ².
questions.incorrectFeedback: Var(2X) = 2²σ² = 4σ², while independent copies add their variances: Var(X₁ + X₂) = 2σ². Same mean, different spread.
